title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: ‘Digital detox’ trend grows, as 55% delete apps and 43% take a break from social media
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**LOGGING OFF FOR A BETTER LIFE**


Digital fatigue is fueling demand for more tactile, human-centered experiences, according to[The Human Advantage report](https://www.quad.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Quad-and-THP-Return-of-Touch-The-Human-Advantage.pdf) from Harris Poll and Quad.


- 75% of Americans say “digital detox” – a simpler relationship with technology – is a lifestyle upgrade.
- 53% intentionally turn off or leave behind their phones to be more present with others.
- 55% are deleting apps from their phones or devices, and 43% have taken a total break from social media.
- 49% of Gen Z say social scrolling leaves them feeling drained – especially texting (41%), emailing (33%) and using AI tools (33%).
- 82% of Gen Z report that taking breaks from social media improves their mental health – up 6 points from last year.
- Physical experiences are gaining appeal: 84% say owning physical items is more satisfying than owning digital ones.
- Collecting things is a growing hobby: 79% of Gen Z say collecting physical objects helps them feel more connected to the real world.
- 68% of Americans currently collect at least one type of physical item, including apparel/sneakers (28%), toys/figures (26%), movie media (24%) and trading cards (22%).
- 80% of Americans are drawn to real-world experiences that do not revolve around screens.
- 84% of Gen Z have gone out of their way for an in-person shopping experience, such as visiting a flagship store or attending a special event.


**BUDGET-CONSCIOUS HOLIDAY SEASON**


More Americans are putting off holiday travel, gift budgets are down, and saving money is a hot topic for shoppers, based on new Harris Poll research with[NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/credit-cards/studies/holiday-spending-report) .


- 31% say they won’t spend money on flights and hotels for holiday travel this year, compared with 22% last year.
- Americans planning to buy gifts expect to spend $879, on average. That’s down 21% from $1,107, on average, last year.
- Using coupons (42%) and shopping sales (41%) are among holiday spenders’ top strategies to save money.
- Gen Z is especially frugal: 33% who will purchase gifts plan to spend $100 or less, and homemade gifts are popular. Among Gen Z, 27% plan to make a gift for at least one person, compared with 21% of Millennials, 19% of Gen X and 11% of Boomers.


**INVESTORS HAVE ELECTION ANXIETY**


Investors are increasingly rattled by the U.S. midterm elections, even as advisors urge them to stay focused on the long term, according to new Harris Poll research with[Nationwide.](https://news.nationwide.com/download/d00600dd-7799-4e72-9783-f4c2a50bc996/nfm-25819aomidtermelectiondatadeck.pdf)


- 40% of investors have changed their retirement savings or portfolio ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
- 3 in 4 people believe the election outcome could meaningfully affect their long-term financial plan.
- 56% say the upcoming midterms are making them more anxious.
- Among those making changes, 15% moved money into more conservative or lower-risk investments, and 13% diversified into new asset classes or sectors.
- 72% of Gen Z have adjusted their retirement savings or portfolio in anticipation of the election, compared with 17% of Baby Boomers.
- *See also:[Nearly 61% believe country is in recession and 65% of independents say economy is worse, according to new Harris poll](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/15/voters-economy-cost-of-living-prices-poll)*


**WORKERS ARE ADAPTING, YET NOT THRIVING**


Workers are regaining confidence by adapting to today’s nonstop change, yet most still lack a healthy relationship with work, according to the[Work Relationship Index 2026](https://www.hp.com/content/dam/sites/worldwide/wri/WRI_2026_Global_Report.pdf) from National Research Group and HP.


- 29% of professionals report a healthy relationship with work, up from 21% in 2025.
- At the same time, 71% remain in the “critical” or “watch-out” zones.
- 49% of business leaders and 41% of IT decision makers report a healthy relationship with their work.
- Only 27% of Gen X report a positive relationship with work, the lowest of any generation, behind Boomers at 29% and seven points lower than Gen Z and Millennials.
- 67% of professionals say it feels too risky to leave their job right now.
- 36% have an income-generating side hustle or venture, rising to 48% among Gen Z.
- 47% of all workers use AI agents, and workers with a healthy work relationship are more likely to use AI agents.
- *See also:[90% of U.S. technology leaders are using AI to produce more while maintaining or expanding engineering headcount](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261008972881/en/AI-Is-Making-Top-Engineers-More-Valuable-as-Companies-Use-Productivity-Gains-to-Produce-More-Software-New-Karat-Research-Finds)*
